data.turoyo: omər azzən qṭəlle manṭalle mawfaqqe, komər mḥalaqqe tamo, mqasqasse hawxa, komər aṯyo li ʕamṯo maltamla ap parčayat diḏe kulle w maḥtila b qotiye hawxa b sanduqo w marfalla.
data.translation: Sie gingen hin, töteten ihn und holten ihn heraus. Sie warfen ihn zur Seite, (nachdem) sie ihn zerstückelt hatten. Da kam die Tante, sammelte alle seine Stücke, tat sie in eine Schachtel, eine Kiste, und ließ sie davon(schwimmen).

rationale: Thin Preterit cell; source s-spelling retained and body-parts context makes the meaning recoverable.

data.translation: Sie ergriffen ihren Großvater und hackten ihn in Stücke.

rationale: Thin Preterit cell; overt grandfather patient in a complete short sentence.

data.turoyo: Gənwət laḥmo me emox, kəmqaṣqəṣatle bag garme, kobatle lu kumsoḥro, kəmtawtaḥle li mʕarṯo — u laḥmo.
data.translation: Du stiehlst deiner Mutter Brot, zermalmst es mit Knochen gibst es einem Rotkopf, und der lässt es in eine Höle hinunterfallen. (Das Brot; die Knochen sind die Zähne, der Rotkopf die Zunge).

rationale: Thin Infectum cell; bread is broken with teeth, with the edition's full riddle explanation retained.

data.turoyo: W mu yawmawo hul l adyawma kul d komfaṣanno badle w koṯe u qaṭlo du abrayḏi l boli, kodoʕanno, moyadno laf falqanək, mqaṣqaṣnanne w mḥalaqananne l tamho.
data.translation: Und seit jenem Tage bis heute, so oft ich ein Gewand zuschneide und mir der Mord an meinem Sohne in den Sinn kommt, nehme ich die Stücke wieder, zerschneide sie in Stücke und werfe sie weg.

rationale: Thin Infectum cell; unambiguous first-person repeated fragmentation of cloth.

summary: The glossary labels the quadriliteral stem I; retained throughout. JTM mqasqasse and mqaṣqaṣṣe show source orthographic variants, without changing root identity.

PrS 19/48 Qaṣqaṣle lacks the inherited m- in the same giant-cutting passage cited prs 48/7. Recorded as a textual/formal variant rather than duplicating the near-identical example or normalizing its spelling.

52/189 has explicit repeated first-person destruction of cloth; 52/10 mqaṣqaṣṣe could instead be a homographic Preterit or a bare Infectum with a patient suffix. No confident box addition is made from 52/10.

44/144 and 94/93 are already quoted. 112/146 is already cited alongside the ox example but actually describes a ram; its distinct context is noted for editors rather than silently replacing the inherited reference or animal.
The human fragmentation contexts are already covered by the inherited sword example. Similar meaning alone does not justify conflating source mqatqat- with qṣqṣ.
Is mqaṣqaṣṣe in 52/10 Preterit or bare Infectum with a patient suffix?
Does MAC NE Samson the hero/16 describe severe mutilation or hyperbolic beating? The reader reports later survival, but later verses are not supplied here; do not infer a literal death.
Should 112/146 remain as a parallel citation to the ox example, or receive its own ram quotation?

data.question: Is 112/146 intentionally a supplementary attestation of mqaṣqaṣle?

rationale: The quoted plural nḥərre with the ox u tawro matches 44/144 exactly. At 112/146 a single man slaughters a ram (nḥəlle), and mqaṣqaṣle is also present. The automatic “not-found” result therefore does not establish a bad verb attestation, but this verse is not the source of the full quotation. Confirm whether the secondary citation is intentional.

summary: Bread broken with teeth and cloth cut into fragments preserve the same physical fragmentation sense as flesh or stalks. MAC Samson's 'torn to bits' is potentially hyperbolic rather than proof of a new severe-beating sense.
